title: Jesus Calling: Enjoying Peace in His Presence
author: Sarah Young
target_audience: Christians seeking daily inspiration and encouragement
Individuals interested in deepening their faith and relationship with Jesus
People experiencing stress, anxiety, or longing for peace
core_themes: Finding peace and hope through faith
Hearing God’s voice in quiet moments
primary_purpose: To provide readers with daily, scripture-based encouragement and reassurance, helping them cultivate a sense of peace, closeness with God, and trust in Jesus’s presence through a year-long devotional journey.

structure_format.narrative_style: Personal, first-person devotional (as if Jesus is speaking directly to the reader)
features: Emphasis on reflective and calming language

key_concepts_lessons: Jesus’s peace is available to believers regardless of life’s circumstances.
God desires daily, intimate communication with each individual.
Trust and surrender lead to strength and spiritual growth.
Gratitude and stillness invite God’s presence and comfort.
Personal struggles can be reframed as opportunities to grow closer to God.
notable_features: Written from Jesus’s perspective using first-person narration
International bestseller translated into multiple languages
Widely used in personal devotion and group settings
cultural_historical_context: Released in the early 2000s, 'Jesus Calling' responded to increasing interest in personalized, meditative devotionals. Its distinctive narrative style and focus on experiencing Jesus’s peace resonated with readers coping with stress, uncertainty, and a fast-paced world.
reception_impact: Bestseller in Christian literature with over 40 million copies sold worldwide
Widely praised for its calming influence and encouragement
Some theological debate about the first-person voice and the presentation of Jesus’s words
Inspired a range of spin-off products, journals, and devotionals
comparable_titles: Streams in the Desert by L.B. Cowman
My Utmost for His Highest by Oswald Chambers
New Morning Mercies by Paul David Tripp
